newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian hotel rented instead of privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian hotel rented instead of privatisation.

text.p: The Sahara Palace Hotel for which Tunisia launched in February an international tender for sell off as part of its privatisation programme, has been rented to a privately owned Tunisian tourism firm, officials said on Friday.

They said the 188-bed, five-star hotel in the southern city of Nefta, a gateway to the desert and the oasis of Djerid, was rented by the Groupe Sangho which has several other hotels in southern Tunisia.
"The offers for purchasing were not satisfactory, and the offer for renting it was better," an official said.
Groupe Sangho, headed by businessman Hosni Jemmali, has rented the hotel for 15 years, tourism sources said.
The hotel is owned by Tunisian state-controlled bank Banque Nationale Agricole.
